records.label: Exercise 6.4 · Q2(i)
records.sourceStem: Find the value of θ if
records.englishPrompt:
Find the value of θ if
(i) sin θ = 0.9975
stepsEnglish: To reverse a sine table, find the value 0.9975 in the natural sines table rather than using an inverse-sine calculator.
Near 90°, several adjacent one-minute entries round to the same four-figure value. The table gives 0.9974 at 85°54′ and a 0.0001 mean difference for the small remaining minutes.
Therefore 85°57′, 85°58′ and 85°59′ are all accepted by the prescribed four-figure table and official key. Do not claim a single exact angle.

records.label: Exercise 6.4 · Q2(ii)
records.sourceStem: Find the value of θ if
records.englishPrompt:
Find the value of θ if
(ii) cos θ = 0.6763
stepsEnglish: Find the closest preceding six-minute column in the natural cosines table: cos 47°24′ is tabulated as 0.6769.
Cosine decreases as the acute angle grows. The extra 3′ have mean difference 0.0006, which must be subtracted: 0.6769 − 0.0006 = 0.6763.
The required angle is θ = 47°27′.

records.label: Exercise 6.4 · Q2(iii)
records.sourceStem: Find the value of θ if
records.englishPrompt:
Find the value of θ if
(iii) tan θ = 0.0720
stepsEnglish: Look backwards through the natural tangents table. At 4°06′, the four-figure value is 0.0717.
One extra minute adds a mean difference 0.0003: 0.0717 + 0.0003 = 0.0720.
Therefore θ = 4°7′ (four degrees seven minutes), the angle whose tabulated tangent is 0.0720.

records.label: Exercise 6.4 · Q2(iv)
records.sourceStem: Find the value of θ if
records.englishPrompt:
Find the value of θ if
(iv) cos θ = 0.0410
stepsEnglish: Find 0.0410 using the four-figure natural cosines table. The preceding six-minute column is 87°36′ with value 0.0419.
For the remaining 3′, subtract the cosine mean difference 0.0009: 0.0419 − 0.0009 = 0.0410.
Hence θ = 87°39′, giving the requested four-figure cosine value of 0.0410.

stepsEnglish: Find 7.5958 directly in the natural tangents table.

Therefore θ = 82°30′, read directly from the natural tangent table.

records.label: Exercise 6.4 · Q3(i)
records.sourceStem: Find the value of the following:
records.englishPrompt:
Find the value of the following:
(i) sin 65°39′ + cos 24°57′ + tan 10°10′
stepsEnglish: Read the prescribed four-figure trigonometric tables, including mean differences where the minutes are not an exact six-minute column.
The tabulated values used in the textbook calculation are sin 65°39′ ≈ 0.9111, cos 24°57′ ≈ 0.9066, and tan 10°10′ ≈ 0.1793.
Add the three four-figure table values, not intermediate unrounded calculator values: 0.9111 + 0.9066 + 0.1793 = 1.9970.

records.label: Exercise 6.4 · Q3(ii)
records.sourceStem: Find the value of the following:
records.englishPrompt:
Find the value of the following:
(ii) tan 70°58′ + cos 15°26′ − sin 84°59′
stepsEnglish: Use the prescribed four-figure tables and mean differences; do not silently replace a textbook table entry with an unrounded scientific-calculator value.
The values in the school-table solution are tan 70°58′ ≈ 2.8982, cos 15°26′ ≈ 0.9639, and sin 84°59′ ≈ 0.9962.
Apply the subtraction sign carefully: 2.8982 + 0.9639 − 0.9962 = 3.8621 − 0.9962 = 2.8659. This is the textbook's stated table-method answer; higher-precision calculator evaluation differs.
